html:
A subway line in Tokyo, the oldest underground railway in Asia. Its first stretch, from Asakusa to Ueno, opened on 30 December 1927.

The line was the work of the businessman Hayakawa Noritsugu, who had seen the London Underground and believed Tokyo needed one, especially after the earthquake of 1923 had wrecked the city. His posters sold it as the first subway in the East, and crowds queued for hours to ride the short line. It was extended through Ginza to Shimbashi by 1934, and another company built the stretch on to Shibuya; the two were joined in 1939 after a bitter business fight.

The line runs 14.3 km under some of Tokyo's busiest streets, with small trains drawn by power from a third rail, a mark of its age. Today it is one of thirteen lines in a network that carries millions of riders a day. It set the pattern for metros later built across Asia, from Osaka to the Delhi Metro.
sum: A subway line in Tokyo, the oldest underground railway in Asia. Its first stretch, from Asakusa to Ueno, opened on 30 December 1927.
